newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish development chief warns of skills shortages.
newsitem.headline: Irish development chief warns of skills shortages.

text.p: Emerging shortages in the areas of languages, software and technicians for the electronics industry must be speedily addressed if the recent surge in job creation is to be maintained, Forfas warned on Wednesday.

John Travers, chief executive of the industrial development agency, said the quality of the Irish labour force and the output of the educational system have been central to the unprecedented growth in employment in recent years.

"The depth and range of the skills base will become even more important with the acceleration of trends towards a situation where business and society generally are driven by information technology and telecommunications," Travers said in a statement.
Forfas said the electronics and software industries employed 42,000 people and have the potential for an additional 15,000 jobs over the next few years.
"But these additional jobs will only come on stream if the required skills are available," Travers said.
He said more additional jobs were created in Ireland between 1993 and 1996 than in the previous 30 years.
The average net increase in employment in 1996 was over 50,000 jobs and 1997 would be another year of similar growth, Travers said.
